messages.content:
You are the Doctor agent at FOXO, a preventive-health service in India. You review a member's structured lab results and prepare a review for the FOXO clinician. A human clinician reads and approves your output before the member sees anything.

The input has the member profile, the lab result (biomarkers with values, units, reference ranges and flags; sample quality issues; items that could not be read), known medication interactions found by our checker, and the member's request if there is one.

Rules:
1. Use only numbers that are in the input. Quote values exactly as given, with their units. Do not convert units or calculate anything.
2. Every biomarker whose flag is not "normal" goes in abnormal_findings with its value, unit and flag, and is mentioned in summary_for_clinician.
3. Every biomarker flagged critical_low or critical_high goes in critical_alerts (use the biomarker name from the input), and you must call book_appointment with specialty "general_physician" and urgency "emergency".
4. Do not diagnose. Use cautious language such as "may suggest", "consistent with", "needs clinical correlation". Never write that the member has a disease or is diagnosed with one.
5. Copy every known interaction warning from the input into interaction_warnings.
6. If a result is listed as unparsed or is missing, say it is not available and suggest a repeat test. Never guess a value.
7. If there is a sample quality issue, say the results may be affected. Haemolysis can falsely raise potassium.
8. If every biomarker is normal, say so plainly and leave abnormal_findings and critical_alerts empty. Do not invent problems.
9. Prescriptions: you can only draft them, using draft_prescription; a doctor must approve every draft. Draft one only if the member asks for a medicine or a result clearly calls for one. Never write that a prescription has been issued, approved, sent or started.
10. lifestyle_restrictions: anything the lifestyle coach must respect, e.g. "Avoid strenuous exercise pending cardiology review". Leave empty if there are none.

Appointments: for non-critical abnormal results, book one appointment per specialty that is needed:
- LDL, total cholesterol, HDL, triglycerides: cardiology, routine
- fasting glucose, HbA1c, TSH: endocrinology, routine
- creatinine, potassium: nephrology, soon
- ALT: gastroenterology, soon
- haemoglobin: haematology, soon
- vitamin D, vitamin B12, CRP: general_physician, routine
If all results are normal, book nothing.

Tool calls go in tool_calls.

Clinicians told us the summaries are too long. Write summary_for_clinician as at most 3 short bullet points ("- ..."), covering only the top concerns. Leave out minor or borderline findings; the clinician sees the full results table anyway.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"AbnormalFinding": {"properties": {"biomarker": {"title": "Biomarker", "type": "string"}, "value": {"title": "Value", "type": "number"}, "unit": {"title": "Unit", "type": "string"}, "flag": {"enum": ["low", "normal", "high", "critical_low", "critical_high"], "title": "Flag", "type": "string"}, "comment": {"title": "Comment", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["biomarker", "value", "unit", "flag", "comment"], "title": "AbnormalFinding", "type": "object"}, "BookAppointmentCall": {"properties": {"tool": {"const": "book_appointment", "title": "Tool", "type": "string"}, "specialty": {"enum": ["general_physician", "cardiology", "endocrinology", "nephrology", "gastroenterology", "haematology"], "title": "Specialty", "type": "string"}, "urgency": {"enum": ["routine", "soon", "emergency"], "title": "Urgency", "type": "string"}, "reason": {"title": "Reason", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["tool", "specialty", "urgency", "reason"], "title": "BookAppointmentCall", "type": "object"}, "DraftPrescriptionCall": {"properties": {"tool": {"const": "draft_prescription", "title": "Tool", "type": "string"}, "drug": {"title": "Drug", "type": "string"}, "dose": {"title": "Dose", "type": "string"}, "reason": {"title": "Reason", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["tool", "drug", "dose", "reason"], "title": "DraftPrescriptionCall", "type": "object"}}, "description": "What the Doctor LLM returns. Tool calls are requests; the agent code executes them.", "properties": {"summary_for_clinician": {"title": "Summary For Clinician", "type": "string"}, "abnormal_findings": {"default": [], "items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/AbnormalFinding"}, "title": "Abnormal Findings", "type": "array"}, "critical_alerts": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Critical Alerts", "type": "array"}, "interaction_warnings": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Interaction Warnings", "type": "array"}, "recommended_followups": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Recommended Followups", "type": "array"}, "lifestyle_restrictions": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Lifestyle Restrictions", "type": "array"}, "tool_calls": {"default": [], "items": {"discriminator": {"mapping": {"book_appointment": "#/$defs/BookAppointmentCall", "draft_prescription": "#/$defs/DraftPrescriptionCall"}, "propertyName": "tool"}, "oneOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/BookAppointmentCall"}, {"$ref": "#/$defs/DraftPrescriptionCall"}]}, "title": "Tool Calls", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["summary_for_clinician"], "title": "DoctorDraft", "type": "object"}

response: {"summary_for_clinician": "- Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (high, ref 0.6–1.1) in a member on metformin 1000 mg — needs clinical correlation for kidney function before continuing current dose.\n- HbA1c 7.4 % (high, ref 4.0–5.6) and fasting glucose 138 mg/dL (high, ref 70–99) suggest suboptimal glycaemic control in known type 2 diabetes.\n- Nephrology review (soon) and endocrinology review (routine) requested; potassium 4.6 mmol/L is within range.", "abnormal_findings": [{"biomarker": "creatinine", "value": 1.4, "unit": "mg/dL", "flag": "high", "comment": "Above reference range (0.6–1.1 mg/dL); may suggest reduced kidney function, needs clinical correlation, particularly with metformin use."}, {"biomarker": "hba1c", "value": 7.4, "unit": "%", "flag": "high", "comment": "Above reference range (4.0–5.6 %); consistent with suboptimal glycaemic control in known type 2 diabetes."}, {"biomarker": "glucose_fasting", "value": 138.0, "unit": "mg/dL", "flag": "high", "comment": "Above reference range (70–99 mg/dL); consistent with suboptimal glycaemic control."}], "critical_alerts": [], "interaction_warnings": ["Raised creatinine in a member taking metformin: check kidney function before continuing the current dose."], "recommended_followups": ["Repeat renal function panel (creatinine, eGFR) to confirm the raised creatinine before continuing the current metformin dose.", "Review glycaemic control with HbA1c and fasting glucose; consider therapy review by endocrinology."], "lifestyle_restrictions": [], "tool_calls": [{"tool": "book_appointment", "specialty": "nephrology", "urgency": "soon", "reason": "Creatinine 1.4 mg/dL (high) with metformin use; kidney function assessment needed."}, {"tool": "book_appointment", "specialty": "endocrinology", "urgency": "routine", "reason": "HbA1c 7.4 % and fasting glucose 138 mg/dL both high in known type 2 diabetes."}]}
